test_title: PYST 31: SSC CHSL - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 20 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A man spends Rs. 2,300 monthly on average for the first four months and Rs. 1,800 monthly for the next eight months and saves Rs. 12,400 a year. Find his monthly income.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Monthly Income** = (Total Yearly Expenditure + Yearly Savings) ÷ 12

Total Yearly Expenditure = (4 × 2300) + (8 × 1800) = 9200 + 14400 = Rs. 23,600

Total Yearly Income = 23,600 + 12,400 = Rs. 36,000

Monthly Income = 36,000 ÷ 12 = Rs. 3,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average expenditure for first 4 months = Rs. 2,300

Average expenditure for next 8 months = Rs. 1,800

Total **annual savings** = Rs. 12,400

**Formula Used:**

Total Income = Total Expenditure + Total Savings

Monthly Income = Total Annual Income ÷ 12

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c95ef8a1b33325e311f42f276e176148107c20cd5bf26f96ec17de8f24512f5.png] 

⇒ Total Expenditure for first 4 months = 4 × 2300 = Rs. 9,200

⇒ Total Expenditure for next 8 months = 8 × 1800 = Rs. 14,400

⇒ Total Annual Expenditure = 9,200 + 14,400 = Rs. 23,600

⇒ Total Annual Income = Annual Expenditure + Annual Savings

⇒ Total Annual Income = 23,600 + 12,400 = Rs. 36,000

⇒ **Monthly Income** = 36,000 ÷ 12 = Rs. 3,000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Relationship

The fundamental relation is **Income = Expenditure + Savings**. Any change in one parameter directly affects the others when the third is constant.

Weighted Average

When calculating average for different periods, use the weighted average formula: **Avg = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)**, where n represents the number of months.

Unit Consistency

Always ensure the time periods match. If savings are given **annually**, convert expenditures to an annual sum before calculating monthly income.</p
